messages:
maya: Opening a PR to add a 'sample prompts' section + compatibility notes for Aurora-Lite-4B in the model catalog. Also adding an SDK snippet for streaming outputs. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/4321. Ping @alex @sam for limits + bench link.

alex: on it, will check sequence limits and quantized compat. do we have bench numbers for 2k vs 8k?

sam: ran a quick cogbench yesterday — 2k median latency ~45ms/token, 8k ~180ms/token on a single GPU; i'll upload the csv.

sam: uploading bench CSV -> https://internal.storage/benches/aurora-lite-4b-2026-03-21.csv

devrel-bot: Checklist: docs PR template passed, markdown linter ok, code-snippet formatting OK.

maya: SDK snippet i'm proposing:

```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
with client.stream_generate('aurora-lite-4b', prompt='Translate this to French: Hello world') as stream:
    for chunk in stream:
        print(chunk.text, end='')
```

please sanity-check.

alex: two quick notes: add a 'quantized CPU fallback' compatibility note (Aurora-Lite-4B supports 4-bit quant on x86 only with kernel v2.1+), and set max_sequence to 8192 in the card. also link to runtime compat matrix: https://go.redwood/runtime-compat

maya: thanks — will add: "quantized CPU fallback supported; expect ~2x latency vs GPU" and bump max_sequence to 8192.

jordan: for sample prompts can we include a tiny example handling streaming interruptions? UX will want a reconnect/resume pattern.

maya: good call — adding a reconnect snippet below the streaming example.

maya: reconnect snippet idea:

```python
# naive resume example
try:
    with client.stream_generate('aurora-lite-4b', prompt=prompt) as s:
        for c in s:
            print(c.text, end='')
except ConnectionError:
    # re-open stream and request continuation token
    with client.stream_generate('aurora-lite-4b', prompt=prompt, resume_from=last_token) as s:
        for c in s:
            print(c.text, end='')
```

priya: tiny nit: prefer 'Translate this to French:' (capitalization + full word) in the user-facing prompt.

maya: updated phrasing in the PR. @sam can you confirm the bench link is stable and provide p50/p95 numbers so i can cite them?

sam: link is good. p50 = 22 tok/s at 2k, p95 = 9 tok/s at 8k. added these to the PR under 'benchmarks (median/p95)'.

alex: LGTM on content and phrasing. i'll do a final pass for compatibility language and merge labels later today.

maya: thanks all — i'll mark the PR docs/ready-for-merge once alex approves. (reacts :thumbsup:)
